intro: If you need a no-fuss Bangkok base with free parking, spacious rooms, and easy access to a major mall — imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok (formerly The Pantip Hotel Ladprao) delivers exactly that. This 3-star, 212-room hotel under the Imperial Hotels group sits on Soi Ladprao 127 in Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi. The Mall Lifestore Bang Kapi is a short drive away, the Yellow Line MRT's Lam Sali station is nearby, and Suvarnabhumi Airport is reachable in about 20 minutes. Guest score: 7.9 out of 10 from 280 reviews on Trip.com. Rates from approx. ฿700/night.

body.html: imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok isn't trying to be anything other than what it is: a practical, honest-value 3-star hotel in Bangkok's eastern residential belt. The 212-room property — run under the Imperial Hotels banner and formerly known as The Pantip Hotel Ladprao — has been a quiet constant on Soi Ladprao 127 for years. The Bang Kapi neighbourhood is not a tourist hotspot, and that's precisely the point: you get a big room, free parking, and calm surroundings for far less than you'd pay in the city centre, with the tools to get anywhere you need.

Location works best for guests who know what they're here for. The Mall Lifestore Bang Kapi — a full-scale mall with HarborLand indoor waterpark, cinema, supermarket, and a dense food court — is a five-minute drive. The Yellow Line MRT's Lam Sali station is accessible by a short ride, connecting onward to Ratchadaphisek, On Nut, and the wider BTS network. Suvarnabhumi Airport sits roughly 20–25 minutes away by road, making this a viable overnight stop before or after an early flight. The Saen Saeb express canal boat, running from a nearby pier, cuts through Bangkok traffic to reach the old city in under an hour.
"Room was bigger than expected, very clean. Free parking at the back was a lifesaver. Staff at front desk were genuinely helpful — sorted everything without fuss."

The room lineup runs from Superior and Deluxe categories to One- and Two-Bedroom Suites for families or groups. Guest reviews consistently note that room sizes feel generous for the price bracket — comfortable beds, reliable air conditioning, flat-screen TV, in-room safe, and free Wi-Fi throughout. Free parking at the rear of the building is a standout feature for Bangkok: street parking in this district is becoming scarce, and having it included at no extra charge is something guests mention repeatedly in positive reviews.

On-site facilities include a restaurant serving an American-style breakfast buffet (06:00–10:00), with Halal meals available on request. A fitness room, business centre, meeting rooms, and 24-hour front desk cover the basics for both leisure and corporate guests. Room service and laundry are available. The hotel suits solo travellers, business visitors to the Bang Kapi district, and families looking for a cost-efficient base with easy road and transit connections to the rest of Bangkok.

Honesty demands acknowledging the recurring concerns in guest reviews. The hotel sits near a wet market, and the smell of fresh seafood and produce can drift in during early morning hours — particularly noticeable through open windows or when walking on the lower floors near the market side. Multiple reviews flag this as a real issue, not a minor quibble. Elevator reliability has also been cited: at least two separate reviews mention lifts being out of service for consecutive days, requiring guests to use the stairs. Soundproofing between some rooms is thin, and a handful of reviewers noted staff attitude varying depending on the time of day or staff member.

The overall picture: imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok is a reliable budget-to-midrange pick for the Bang Kapi area. For ฿700–฿900 per night in low season (rising during peak periods and festivals), you get a spacious room, free parking, and a workable location for anyone with business on Bangkok's eastern side. The Mall, canal boats, Yellow Line MRT, and Suvarnabhumi Airport form a practical web of connections from here. Don't expect a polished boutique experience — but if the basics are what you need, this hotel delivers them without pretence.

highlights.title: Near The Mall Bang Kapi
highlights.text: The Mall Lifestore Bang Kapi — with HarborLand waterpark, cinema, supermarket and food court — is a 5-minute drive. Shopping and dining are never far.

highlights.title: Free On-Site Parking
highlights.text: Free private parking at the rear of the hotel — a genuine advantage in Bang Kapi where street parking is increasingly scarce. No extra charge for the whole stay.

highlights.title: Yellow Line MRT Access
highlights.text: The Lam Sali MRT station (Yellow Line) is a short ride away, connecting onward to Ratchadaphisek and the BTS/MRT network for city-wide travel.

honestSummary: imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok delivers honest 3-star value in a practical Bang Kapi location — spacious rooms, free parking, friendly staff, from around ฿700/night. The wet-market smell and occasional elevator issues are real, recurring concerns that guests should know about before booking.
honestChecks: If you're sensitive to morning food market odours or need complete quiet — the hotel's proximity to a wet market means smells can drift in early. Request a room on a higher floor or facing the main road when booking.
If you need a pool or full leisure facilities — imm hotel has no swimming pool. Consider Metro Point Bangkok Hotel or 130 Hotel & Residence, both in the same district with additional amenities.
If you want to walk to Bangkok's main tourist areas — Bang Kapi is a residential district; you'll need the MRT or Grab for Sukhumvit, Silom, or the old city. Plan travel time accordingly.

tips.title: Request a room facing the main road
tips.body: To avoid early-morning smells from the nearby wet market, ask for a room on a higher floor or facing the main street rather than the market side. A small request that makes a real difference.

tips.title: Yellow Line MRT + Saen Saeb canal boat
tips.body: The Yellow Line MRT at Lam Sali connects to Ratchadaphisek and the BTS network. The Saen Saeb express boat from a nearby pier cuts through Bangkok traffic — two good alternatives to Grab.

tips.title: Eat outside — Bang Kapi has great street food
tips.body: Bang Kapi market, the noodle and rice stalls on surrounding sois, and the Sammakon Ram 110 cafe-restaurant strip are all close. Skip the hotel restaurant for at least one meal and explore the neighbourhood.

tips.title: Ideal night-before-flight base
tips.body: Suvarnabhumi Airport is about 20–25 minutes by road (off-peak). imm hotel's rates are significantly lower than airport hotels, making it a smart choice for an early-morning departure.

faqTitle: FAQ — imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok

faq.q: Where is imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok located?
faq.a: The hotel is at 3191 Soi Ladprao 127, Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi, Bangkok 10240. It's about a 5-minute drive from The Mall Lifestore Bang Kapi, and roughly 5 minutes to the Yellow Line MRT Lam Sali station. Suvarnabhumi Airport is approximately 20–25 minutes by road.

faq.q: Does imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok have free parking?
faq.a: Yes — free private parking is available at the rear of the hotel for guests throughout their stay. This is one of the hotel's key selling points, particularly for travellers arriving by car in a district where parking is becoming harder to find.

faq.q: What is the price range at imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok?
faq.a: Standard Superior Rooms start from approximately ฿700/night during low season. Deluxe Rooms run around ฿900, One Bedroom Suites from ฿1,300, and Two Bedroom Suites from ฿1,800. Rates rise during holidays and peak periods — always compare platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is imm hotel the same as The Pantip Hotel Ladprao Bangkok?
faq.a: Yes, they are the same property. The Pantip Hotel Ladprao Bangkok rebranded as imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok under the Imperial Hotels group. The address, ownership, and management remain the same.

faq.q: Who is imm hotel Ladprao Bangkapi Bangkok best suited for?
faq.a: Best for business travellers with meetings in Bang Kapi, families or groups arriving by car, and cost-conscious travellers wanting a comfortable room near The Mall Bang Kapi and easy access to Suvarnabhumi Airport. Less suited to visitors who want to walk to Bangkok's main tourist districts — you'll need public transit or a ride-hail app.
